approach: Write one design file, docs/design/hestia.md, with a table of the eight failures (check, code or model, cadence, fix or report), then budget, measures, Hades fold-in and split rule, alternatives, the Artemis boundary, and a numbered build plan of one-producer jobs with deterministic checks first. Append D129 (proposed) at the very end of docs/decisions.md. Add one CHANGELOG line under Unreleased. Add a short Hestia pointer to the roadmap. Leave decision-links.toml alone unless the new entry uses a link phrase. No code, athena.toml or defaults.toml changes.

decisions.choice: Hestia is a rules-first sweep: code finds and measures, a model only judges the two fuzzy checks (queued request done or superseded; docs that no longer match code) and its output is a report, never a deletion.
decisions.reason: Six of the eight failures are checkable facts (git, filesystem, file mtimes, byte counts, config grep). A model reading the rest keeps cost low and results reproducible, in line with D127's rules-first shape.

rejected.why: Costly, not reproducible, and misses plain facts like a full cache directory.
Cannot tell whether a queued request is already done or a doc still matches the code.

decisions.choice: Hestia reports and makes small fixes only through the normal job pipeline; destructive cleanup is limited to branches, worktrees and caches provably Athena's own and already merged, everything else becomes a work item.
decisions.reason: D127 says Hestia does not gate work; direct edits would bypass verification. Reporting an uncertain deletion costs little, a wrong deletion is irreversible.

rejected.why: Leaves obvious tidying (a merged branch, a stale build cache) to pile up, as the 2026-10-23 disk fill shows.

decisions.choice: Hades's cleanup is a module of Hestia for now (a 'retire' check group), splitting out when rollback or deprecation work exists, or when cleanup findings exceed half of all findings over 4 weeks (an estimate to tune).
decisions.reason: There is no rollback or deprecation workload yet; a separate role would add a prompt set and budget for one check group.

rejected.why: Adds a role with a prompt budget for work that is mostly deterministic cleanup.

rejected.option: Fold into the D127 scope guard
rejected.why: D127 and its Alternatives (b) keep continuity apart from throttling work; blurs gate and tidy.

decisions.choice: Append D129 at the end of docs/decisions.md with status proposed, avoiding the phrases 'supersedes', 'superseded by' and 'amends'.
decisions.reason: The log is append-only and hash-pinned over its first 230046 bytes (crates/athena-cli/src/decisions.rs tests); those phrases create backtest hits that must be listed in docs/decision-links.toml, whose entries are keyed by line number.

rejected.option: Insert the entry in the middle or beside D127
rejected.why: Breaks the pinned prefix hash and was the D128 defect.

decisions.choice: Findings are measured by resolved problems and time from appearance to resolution, plus true-positive rate on a spot check; an empty findings list is always reported with the checks that ran.
decisions.reason: Matches the outcome-check and no-empty-success defaults; sweep counts alone measure activity.

rejected.option: Count sweeps run or findings raised

files.purpose: The Hestia design: eight-failure check table, code versus model, cadence, fix or report, budget and stop rule, measures, Hades fold-in and split trigger, alternatives, Artemis boundary, build plan.
Append D129, status proposed, in the neighbouring field format, after D128 and nothing else changed.
One bullet under Unreleased for the design and the proposed decision.
One short line pointing to the Hestia design where continuity work belongs (brief lists it as a deliverable); no row changes.
Only if D129 text must use a supersession or amend phrase; the plan avoids those phrases, so expected unchanged.

steps: Read the end of docs/decisions.md to confirm D128 is last, and BRIEF.md lines 600-610 and the 2026-10-25 addendum for exact wording to cite.

Write docs/design/hestia.md: purpose and reader, definitions of Hestia, Hades and each failure in plain terms, the eight-row table (check, code or model, cadence, fix or report), the empty-findings rule, a fix-by-small-job versus report rule with the provably-Athena's-own limit on deletion.
Add budget (dollars and wall time per run and in total, stop rule, all labeled estimates), measures, Hades fold-in and split trigger, alternatives, Artemis boundary with D127 and BRIEF.md citations.

Add the build plan: numbered jobs, each one producer run, with deliverables, test, dependencies; deterministic checks first (branches/worktrees/caches, unpushed checkpoints, binary age, budget headroom, keep rule, propose age), then queue-state and doc-drift model checks, then fix-job emission and measures.
Append D129 · Hestia continuity role (proposed) at the end of docs/decisions.md with Status, Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost, Provenance.
Add the CHANGELOG bullet under Unreleased and a one-line pointer in docs/design/roadmap.md.
Run cargo fmt --all --check and cargo test --locked; fix any link or policy failures.

risks.risk: Editing earlier bytes of docs/decisions.md breaks the pinned prefix hash test.
risks.mitigation: Append only after the final line of D128; do not touch other text.

risks.risk: Phrases like 'supersedes' or 'amends' in D129 or hestia.md create unlisted backtest hits.
risks.mitigation: Avoid these words in D129; run cargo test and, if a hit appears, add a link entry by line number.

risks.risk: Banned words or email-like text in new docs fail the policy scan.
risks.mitigation: Write plain role names only; no operator or machine names, no addresses.
Label each number 'estimate' or give its source; state the request-supplied figures as stated.

risks.risk: Prompt budget test fails if docs counted in always-loaded sets change.
risks.mitigation: New files sit outside the role prompt sets; run cargo test to confirm system_facts_budgets_match_computed.

demonstrations.method: Read the check table in docs/design/hestia.md and confirm eight rows each with check, code or model, cadence, fix or report.
demonstrations.command: Grep -n for 'queued request', 'branch', 'worktree', '2026-10-23', 'checkpoint', 'installed binary', 'budget', 'keep rule', 'athena propose', 'docs' in docs/design/hestia.md; Read the table
demonstrations.observes: Eight rows, each with all four fields; the leftover-cache row cites the 2026-10-23 disk-full cache; the doc-drift and queue rows are marked model-assisted, the rest deterministic.
demonstrations.fails_without: A missing row or empty field would leave one of the eight failures with no check, so it would go unnoticed again.

demonstrations.method: Read the budget, measures and Hades sections.
demonstrations.observes: Dollars and wall time per run and in total, a stop rule, each number labeled estimate or sourced, measures (findings per run, spot-check true-positive rate, time to resolution), the fold-in and the split trigger, and the empty-findings rule.
demonstrations.fails_without: Without the stop rule or labels a reviewer could not tell a measured figure from a guess.

demonstrations.method: Read the alternatives and boundary sections and check each cited source exists (BRIEF.md pantheon table at line 603-606, D127).
demonstrations.observes: At least model-only, separate Hades now, and fold into the D127 guard are listed with reasons; the Artemis boundary says Hestia reports and does not gate; citations resolve.
demonstrations.fails_without: No alternatives or boundary would leave the role open to creeping into gating.

demonstrations.method: Check that D129 is the last top-level heading, status proposed, with Case, Decision, Alternatives, Tradeoff, Reversal cost and Provenance bullets, and that the pinned-prefix test passes.
demonstrations.command: Grep -n '^## D12[89]' docs/decisions.md; Read the tail of docs/decisions.md; cargo test --locked -p athena-cli decisions
demonstrations.observes: One new '## D129 · ' heading after D128, 'proposed' in its Status, all fields present; the log guard test the_decision_log_is_well_formed_and_only_appended_to passes.
demonstrations.fails_without: An entry placed inside another or without Provenance fails the log guard test.

demonstrations.observes: Numbered jobs, each with deliverables, a test or behavior check, dependencies and a one-producer size, with deterministic checks (branches, worktrees, caches, unpushed checkpoints, binary age, budgets, keep rule, propose) before model-assisted ones.
demonstrations.fails_without: Unordered or unsized jobs could not be queued as single producer runs.

demonstrations.method: Compare changed files to the allowed list and read the CHANGELOG diff against neighbouring entries.
demonstrations.observes: Changes only in docs/design/hestia.md, docs/decisions.md, CHANGELOG.md, docs/design/roadmap.md; a bullet under [Unreleased] in the existing style; no .rs, athena.toml or defaults.toml in the diff.
demonstrations.fails_without: A code or governance file in the diff would break the no-code scope.

demonstrations.method: Run both from the repository root.
demonstrations.observes: Both pass, including the decision-log guard, backtest link check, budgets test and the boundary-word scan over the new files.
demonstrations.fails_without: A modified old entry, a stray supersession phrase without a link, or a banned word or email in the new text would fail these tests.

open_questions: The figures in the request (disk fill on 2026-10-23, stale binary, unpushed checkpoints, nearly full budgets, 49 open requests) come from the request; records/ is absent, so the design cites them as stated.
Whether the roadmap should gain a row or only a pointer; the plan chooses a pointer to keep the change small.
Where Hestia's cadence is triggered (a drain hook, a timer, or athena command) is not settled from code and is left to build job 1.
